findings.text: follow-on: a code review composed with --path alone is never stored. store_delivered_reviews is the only caller of delivered_code_reviews and passes around=plan_slug, and the keep filter at plan_review.py:2198 requires sidecar["around"] == around, so a path-only subject (around="") is composed and dispatched but its delivered report is never read into the store, though the plan's section 6 deliverable names both subjects and store_code_review is otherwise unreachable.

follow-on: assert record["neighbourhood_key"] == key compares the stored key against key = plan_review.code_review_key(...) at line 262, the same function the write path uses, so both sides move together and the assertion survives a regression in code_review_key (for example a constant key); no independent literal pins the neighbourhood key.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against 4e4de5ba; the change composes the health brief for a neighbourhood, dispatches one read-only review node, and stores the delivered report keyed by the neighbourhood, and the store keeps code reviews out of the plan-review listing (PLAN_REVIEW_FILE_GLOB is plan-*.v*.json).
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names tests/test_review_composes_a_code_subject.py; the manifest records 5 passed EXIT=0 and the file asserts the measure (neighbourhood names reckon/a.py and reckon.b and not reckon.c, carries the stored finding and the four interface-figure keys, and review-plan composes the same plan brief as review).
item_verdicts.goal: the source node's goal is "Compose a code review around a plan or a path through one review verb"; the landed change adds crew review with --around/--path and composes a code neighbourhood brief at reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:2116, resolving it through code_review_subject and dispatch_code_review in reckon/crew/plan_review.py.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the gate (49 passed, EXIT=0), the declared negative control (1 failed 4 passed, EXIT=1 on assert "reckon.b" in neighbourhood) and the two population arms (5 failed base, 5 failed head) with their log paths.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the node declared six paths (reckon/crew/plan_review.py, reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py, reckon/cli.py, tests/test_review_composes_a_code_subject.py, the evidence fragment and the figures dir); the diff additionally edits reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py, tests/test_crew_help_names_its_state.py and four review-plan test files, each recorded in the manifest as a review-granted fence extension.

justifications.durability: the neighbourhood assertion is a real guard (negative-control-2.log reddens it on the mutation), but the store-key assertion at tests/test_review_composes_a_code_subject.py:272 is circular and no test stores a path-only review.
justifications.evidence: the gate at gate-2.log names tests/test_review_composes_a_code_subject.py (5 passed) and the negative control at negative-control-2.log:175 reproduces the named failure at EXIT=1.
justifications.fit: the module follows the surrounding plan_review.py idiom and names nothing the naming rules forbid, though it reaches two private helpers across modules (_review_dispatch_tokens, fleet_index._git_head).
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:2112-2124 composes and dispatches a code subject through the same _run_review body the plan subject uses, so one verb serves both subjects.
justifications.reuse: each added definition extends an owner — neighbourhood (reckon/served_code.py:1013), parse_health_review (reckon/crew/review.py:1024), write_review_sidecar and review_store_root — and no second import walker or argv builder exists in plan_review.py.
justifications.scope_discipline: every diff path is inside the declared six or a manifest-recorded review extension, but the live pointer did not carry the extension so check-manifest still names two of them.
